approachQuestion.prompt:
For every unordered pair of different positions in an array, measure how many bit positions differ between their values. Return the sum of these distances over all pairs. Equal values at different positions still form a pair.

Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000; values are unsigned 32-bit words; return an exact unsigned 64-bit total.
Example: [1,2,3] -> 4: pair distances are 2,1,1. Edge case: [7,7] -> 0.

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: Word operations on 32-bit inputs and 64-bit totals take constant time. Popcount, if used, takes constant time per 32-bit word.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: At each of the 32 positions count c set bits, then add c*(n-c) to a 64-bit total.
options.feedback: Exactly the pairs crossing from a one to a zero differ at this position. Each unordered pair is counted once per differing bit.

options.text: Allocate an n-by-32 bit table, then sum set-count times clear-count in each column.
options.feedback: It computes the same exact contributions, but materializes bits that can be counted while reading.
That counts ordered pairs. For [0,1], the required total is 1, while this returns 2.

options.text: Enumerate all unordered index pairs and popcount their XOR.
options.feedback: This is correct but explicitly inefficient: it enumerates every pair although each bit contribution can be counted once across the array.

feedback.reason: For one bit with c ones, every differing unordered pair chooses one of c one-positions and one of n-c zero-positions: c*(n-c).
details: For each bit position count ones and infer zeros from n. Their product is the number of unordered pairs differing there. Sum these products in a wide accumulator.

For one bit with c ones, every differing unordered pair chooses one of c one-positions and one of n-c zero-positions: c*(n-c). No division by two is needed because that choice already identifies an unordered pair.

“At each of the 32 positions count c set bits, then add c*(n-c) to a 64-bit total.”: Exactly the pairs crossing from a one to a zero differ at this position. Each unordered pair is counted once per differing bit.
“Allocate an n-by-32 bit table, then sum set-count times clear-count in each column.”: It computes the same exact contributions, but materializes bits that can be counted while reading.
“At each position add 2*c*(n-c).”: That counts ordered pairs. For [0,1], the required total is 1, while this returns 2.

“Enumerate all unordered index pairs and popcount their XOR.”: This is correct but explicitly inefficient: it enumerates every pair although each bit contribution can be counted once across the array.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For count-cross-bit-pairs, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the array length; the bit width is fixed at 32.
constraints: Word operations on 32-bit inputs and 64-bit totals take constant time. Popcount, if used, takes constant time per 32-bit word.

feedback.reason: Thirty-two bit counts replace explicit enumeration of all position pairs.
details: Thirty-two scans take linear time in n; the counts and total occupy a constant number of words. The empty case returns zero.
Word operations on 32-bit inputs and 64-bit totals take constant time. Popcount, if used, takes constant time per 32-bit word.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The analyzed method does not retain a table or copy.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This is looser than the bounded number of scans.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The input cannot be processed without scanning it in the worst case.
